questions.q: What does the Transform element do?
options: It deletes every record in a collection
It copies one or more components or variables into a new variable, letting you change values along the way, applied to a whole collection at once
It only works on a single record at a time, like Get Records
It permanently renames fields on an object
questions.explain: Transform copies source data into an auto-generated target variable while changing values, and it applies across an entire collection without a per-item path.

questions.q: What is a 'mapping' in a Transform element?
options: A geographic visualization of record locations
A line connecting a source field directly to a compatible target field
A list of all objects in the org
A type of Decision outcome
questions.explain: A mapping is the line drawn between a source field and a target field, created by clicking each field's connector icon.

questions.q: When a target field doesn't have a direct source to map from, what are the two options available through the fx icon?
options: Loop or Decision
Formula (reference another flow resource) or Value (a static value for every record)
Delete or Create
Import or Export
questions.explain: The fx icon offers Formula, which references another flow resource, or Value, which sets the same static value for every record in the target.

questions.q: According to this lesson's current Salesforce guidance, how does a Transform element's performance compare to a Loop doing the same bulk record update?
options: Transform is roughly 10 times slower than a Loop
They perform identically in every case
Transform is roughly 10 times faster than a Loop performing the same task, and scales better
Loops are always faster for any bulk operation
questions.explain: Salesforce's guidance states Transform elements run about 10x faster than loops doing equivalent work, with better scaling as flows grow more complex.

questions.q: Per this lesson's rule of thumb, when should you still reach for a Loop instead of a Transform?
options: Never — Transform should always be used instead of Loop
Only when each item in the collection needs to call an Action (like sending an email), which Transform can't do
Only when the collection has fewer than 10 records
Only on scheduled flows
questions.explain: The guidance is to use Transform whenever possible, and reserve Loop for cases a Transform genuinely can't handle, such as calling an Action per item.
